# External test fixtures

These are SEPA XML sample files produced by other open-source projects, vendored here as
cross-implementation parser fixtures. They let us prove that our parser reads real-world XML
generated by independent tools, not just our own writer output.

## sepa_king (`sepa_king/`)

Source: https://github.com/salesking/sepa_king (file `spec/examples/`).
License: MIT, Copyright (c) 2013-2022 Georg Leciejewski (Sales King GmbH) and Georg Ledermann.
Reused here under the terms of the MIT License, with attribution.

Files vendored:
- `pain.001.001.03.xml` (legacy ISO credit transfer)
- `pain.001.003.03.xml` (German DK credit transfer variant)

Not vendored: `sepa_king`'s `pain.008.003.02.xml` example uses a placeholder Creditor Identifier
`DE00ZZZ00099999999` whose check digits are `00`, which is never valid under ISO 7064 MOD 97-10
(valid range 02 to 98). Our validation correctly rejects it, so it is unsuitable as a positive
parse fixture. This is a difference in test-data realism, not a defect in either library. The
Swiss `.ch` and `.002.03` / `.008.002.02` variants are out of our supported scope and are not
vendored either.
